subject.title: [Feature]: Non-interactive command to use Codex OAuth for model provider

question: Should OpenClaw accept a non-interactive OpenAI/Codex OAuth import surface, and what leak-resistant contract may handle callback, code, token, or session material?
rationale: The implementation shape changes how sensitive OAuth material enters OpenClaw and cannot be safely chosen from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design a scoped OAuth import contract
options.body: Add a provider-owned import or auth-session contract with explicit validation, redaction, storage, docs, and proof requirements before any implementation PR.

options.title: Prefer device-code automation only
options.body: Keep callback URLs out of env/config and explore whether device-code pairing plus documented scripting covers the instant-setup use case.

options.title: Decline non-interactive OAuth import
options.body: Keep OpenAI/Codex OAuth interactive and tell operators to use API-key auth for fully non-interactive provisioning.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped OAuth import contract
recommendation.body: Add a provider-owned import or auth-session contract with explicit validation, redaction, storage, docs, and proof requirements before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points most strongly to this person across provider auth plugins, non-interactive setup, and provider OAuth seams.
